headline: Citigroup analysts estimate that Meta's Muse AI assistant could bring in more than $27 billion a year by 2030.
score_reason: A bank's forecast, not a result; read through a secondary outlet.
importance_line: Investors and rivals get one bank's view of the money in AI assistants, but it is a forecast built on early figures of 1.8 million daily users and may prove wrong.
summary: bdnews24 reports that Citi's forecast splits into about $23 billion a year in transaction-related revenue and $4.5 billion in subscriptions, resting on its view that personal AI agents are becoming 'the new front door to the internet'. Citi said Muse, which Meta launched on 8 Sep 2026, has had 6.6 million downloads and 1.8 million daily active users so far, and faces competition from assistants by OpenAI, Google and Anthropic.
notes: Reuters page blocked; read bdnews24's account of the Citi note. Reuters carried the same story (headline in the pool); we did not open it. url is the Reuters link from the pool. The $27 billion is an analyst forecast.
